Two nested `if` statements with nothing else between them test one combined condition. Joined with `&&`, the code loses a level of indentation and the whole condition is in one place.

`no-lonely-if` without the `unicorn/` prefix is a different rule. It reports an `if` that is alone in an `else` block.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```js
if (user) {
  if (user.isAdmin) {
    showSettings();
  }
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
if (user && user.isAdmin) {
  showSettings();
}
```

The two cannot be merged when either one has an `else`, or when the outer block does something more:

{/* good */}
```js
if (user) {
  if (user.isAdmin) {
    showSettings();
  }
} else {
  showLogin();
}

if (user) {
  greet(user);
  if (user.isAdmin) {
    showSettings();
  }
}
```
